question: Should Gateway support scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes should that live inside `allowedOrigins` or a dedicated constrained pattern setting?
rationale: This changes which browser-origin WebSocket and trusted-proxy HTTP requests can pass Gateway authorization, so automation should not choose the wildcard grammar or security posture.

options.title: Define constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, docs, audit handling, and allow/reject tests for approved extension or custom-scheme cases before implementation.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Land exact opaque-origin matching separately and defer the changing-extension-ID wildcard request as outside current Gateway policy.

options.title: Allow only extension scheme wildcard
options.body: Support a narrow `chrome-extension://*` case with scheme-specific matching and negative security tests, without generic trailing-prefix matching.

recommendation.title: Define constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, docs, audit handling, and allow/reject tests for approved extension or custom-scheme cases before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the affected Gateway origin checker and has the clearest history on this security boundary.
